    Compute sensitivity, specificity and false positive rate across thresholds

    compute_threshold_metrics.Rd

    This function computes classification performance metrics (sensitivity, specificity and false positive rate) across a sequence of threshold values. Thresholds are generated from the minimum and maximum predicted values, rounded to the nearest 0.5 by default. For each threshold, predicted values are binarised and compared against observed binary labels using a 2×2 confusion matrix. Metrics are returned in a data frame with one row per threshold.

    compute_threshold_metrics(pred_values, obs_values, step = 0.5)

    Arguments

    pred_values

    Numeric vector of predicted values (e.g. logits or probabilities) used to generate threshold-based classifications.

    obs_values

    Binary vector of cooresponding observed binary values. Values are coerced to a factor internally (levels = `0` and `1`).

    step

    Numeric, the increment between threshold values. Defaults to 0.5.

    Value

    A data.frame with columns:

    threshold

    Threshold used to classify predictions.

    sensitivity

    True positive rate (TP / (TP + FN)).

    specificity

    True negative rate (TN / (TN + FP)).

    fpr

    False positive rate (FP / (FP + TN)).

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
thresholds_df <- compute_threshold_metrics(
  pred_values = predictions$prediction_lodds,
  true_labels = predictions$host_status
)
} # }
